newsitem.title: GERMANY: Court rehabilitates Austrian who opposed Hitler.
newsitem.headline: Court rehabilitates Austrian who opposed Hitler.

text.p: A Berlin court has rehabilitated an Austrian Catholic who opposed Adolf Hitler's 1938 annexation of his country 54 years after the Nazis executed him during World War Two, a justice spokeswoman said on Monday.

The spokeswoman said the court had lifted a 1943 Nazi military tribunal verdict convicting Franz Jaegerstaetter for opposing Nazi rule in Austria and as a conscientious objector who refused to fight in the war on religious grounds.

Jaegerstaetter was executed in August 1943. His rehabilitation came a month after the German government said it was launching a new drive to overturn the unjust convictions of anti-Nazi resistance fighters during Hitler's Third Reich.

Germany's 16 federal states are currently responsible for lifting Nazi court verdicts where these were clearly unjust. But the procedure is a legal minefield which has left many of the most glaring cases still unsettled.
The need for action was highlighted most recently by the case of Dietrich Bonhoeffer, a Protestant clergyman executed at a concentration camp in 1945 for opposing Hitler.

Prosecutors applied in March last year for his high treason conviction to be quashed. After months of investigation, a Berlin court ruled it could not pardon Bonhoeffer as a Bavarian law had already exonerated him and his co-conspirators in 1946.
